summary.intent: Evaluate how well the Wisp plugins served front-end work and design ideation on the orin-dx and techworx (pages) sites by mining ~810 sessions, then act on the findings to reduce turns and context cost and get right results on the first run.
summary.outcome: Four investigation agents confirmed the plugins are too rigid for exploratory work and cannot capture visual intent. Four parallel tracks (gate hygiene, measurement, skill routing wording, outcome-level planner) were merged and a ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} path fix was applied across 66 files. Gate retry context was wired into the skills, versions were bumped (ecosystem 4.5.0), and everything was committed locally with `just check` passing; nothing was pushed.

repo: Wisp plugins form a spec-driven lifecycle (weaver, vanguard, scribe/muse, navigator, smith, courier) with typed JSON handoffs in shared/schemas and default-fail gates; there is no browser, screenshot, or visual mode, and spec@1 has no fields for tokens, layout or appearance.

Relative `shared/...` paths in skills and agents fail first reads because `shared` is a symlink and resolves against the skill dir or user cwd. `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/shared/...` is substituted by the host in both skill and agent text and works on the first read (single-run evidence).
Muse docs referenced a ranger accessibility taxonomy that never existed, so implemented a11y was never checked.
The constitution block is copied byte for byte into every agent (ADR 006), so gate rules were placed in each exit-gate's <output> rather than the constitution.
plan@1 never required code; 'exact code' appeared only in description strings. ADR 014 partially supersedes ADR 009 without a schema change.

Version bumps touch plugin.json, README Version line, CHANGELOG, marketplace.json, .claude-plugin/plugin.json and the Codex manifest; run `just claude-manifests-sync`, `just marketplace-sync`, `just versions`, then `just check`.
Only ~2 real top-level sessions per project dir; the other hundreds of jsonl files are subagent transcripts. Plugin agents appeared in only two top-level sessions (orin-dx b8d16e96, pages 24655582).

In the audited work, every spec failed its first gate with 9-23 blockers, up to 9 retries, with non-monotonic blocker counts; gates checked internal consistency but caught no rendered/visual defects, so defects surfaced later by user eye or the 16 Oct audit.

code.finding: Hook now denies blockers or coverage gaps with whitespace-only criterion/kind/finding/location; deliberately does not check evidence citing because escalation_required and missing_mutation_gate blockers legitimately lack a location.
New ~45-line self-check reference (blocker shape, round rules, 10-check checklist) loaded by muse:drafter and scribe:drafter via <load_first>, with inline fallback if the path doesn't resolve.
Had a stale line claiming no plugin wires the hooks; fixed after the merge.

workflow: Parallel tracks in separate worktrees merged cleanly except for append-only conflicts in IMPLEMENTATION-LOG.md and the ADR README index, resolved by keeping both sides with small scripts.

Probe-plugin experiments with `claude -p --plugin-dir` quickly validated host behavior; a control variant was needed because the first probe leaked the answer by listing the root above the relative path.
Planner pilot runs were invalid when the temp project lacked shared/schemas, since agents invented forbidden task keys; fixtures must name the schema path.
Subagent claims were treated as unverified and spot-checked against diffs (e.g. changelog claims for weaver/navigator/ranger) before being written into changelogs.
User's rule of thumb: explore visually and fast first, then spec and test once the design narrows; text-first descriptions of options repeatedly forced the user to ask 'show me'.

friction: Orchestrator ignored the gate's 3-retry escalation and carried on with an 'owner-directed gate pass' without asking the user.
Large 60-130 KB spec and plan files stalled agent streams (17 failed agent tasks, 32 stall mentions).
Specs written before visuals settled caused gate churn, stale numbers (1180px, 252px) and rewrites after the user's visual review; approval in prose failed, and ~66 drawings were needed.
Design decisions were lost across sessions, and the user had to ask for a search of prior sessions.
Ranger exit-gate's first live denial reason was not recorded, so what broke is unknown.
Merge commits needed GPG, requiring the sandbox to be disabled in one track.
Prompt weight grew in some changes (planner prompt, sketch skill) even as output shrank.
open_items: Push and open a draft PR; tagging and publishing left to the user.
Retry rule is untested live; no before/after measurement of gate rounds or tokens, and whether new skill wording raises invocation rates is unmeasured.

Not yet done from the review-slop list: D6 remainder (changeset@3 flat format), D9, D10/D5 dismissed-finding persistence, A2/C8 CI schema validator, B2/B3/B6-B10, C1-C6 and C9 decisions, effect re-measure, and AGENTS.md adoption in Callisto, Caliper and Monokl.
Gate Wave 3 (visual acceptance evidence before gating) and the reasoning-scratchpad cost/cache question (R2, R3, C4) remain; plan@2 with explicit outcome/signature/test fields is deferred.
Implementer behavior with outcome-level plans, challenger on the new plan shape, and Codex behavior are untested.
Other producers (smith:implementer, sentinel:verifier, ranger scanner/adversary, scribe:architect) lack the gate-readiness self-check; ranger/exit-gate may need the context-hygiene load_first line.
Owner should confirm the gate-rule placement versus a constitution amendment (WP-50), the freehand-claim skill set, and the patch versus minor choice for hook-only plugins.
Design gaps from the audit remain unaddressed: browser/screenshot capability kind, visual-intent channel in specs, decision log, supersession handling, and the muse verdict schema alignment.
